summary: The study describes the growth of self-organized CdSe quantum dots (QDs) embedded in ZnSe using atomic layer epitaxy (ALE) at 230 °C, followed by annealing. The QDs were characterized using time-resolved photoluminescence, revealing distinct optical properties and the effects of resonant excitation on the emission behavior.
evidence: The samples were grown on thermally cleaned (100) GaAs by molecular beam epitaxy (MBE) using elemental sources. Prior to the CdSe growth, a ZnSe buffer layer of typically 120 nm was deposited at 300°C and a growth rate of 240 nm h−1. To achieve self-organized QD formation we basically tried two methods: (1) growth via continuous MBE at 300°C until the transition from the initially 2D streaky reflection high-energy electron diffraction (RHEED) to a 3D spotty pattern occurred, and (2) atomic layer epitaxy (ALE) at a reduced temperature of 230°C and subsequent annealing.
